title: Signal Scrubber Board — UX notes and wireframe draft
content:
Purpose and background:
- Lightweight investigation surface meant for first-touch debugging (SRE, mobile eng, SEs) when model requests fail or degrade (timeouts, 5xx, improbable output).
- Goal: make it trivial to answer three questions in < 2 minutes: 1) Is this systemic or isolated? 2) What changed recently (model, routing, infra)? 3) Quick mitigation steps I can take now.

Design principles (guiding constraints):
- Glanceable: show an incidence-level snapshot (severity, impact, sample request) without forcing users to click through logs.
- Signal-first: surface multiple correlated signals (latency spikes, 5xx rate, model-variant churn, KV cache miss rate) side-by-side.
- Actionable: provide one-click mitigations (route-to-fallback, reduce-max-tokens, change-quantization-profile, retry-with-backoff) where safe.
- Repro and context: preserve the exact request, prompt, model version, sequence length, and headers (sanitized) for replays.
- Lightweight annotations: allow rapid hypothesis notes and tagging to feed autocorrelation later.

High-level layout (wireframe verbal spec):
- Global header: breadcrumb (Console > Signals > Signal Scrubber), time-range quick-selector, severity filter, search box (query by request-id, user-id, route).
- Left rail (incident stream): compact list of recent incidents sorted by impact score (combines user volume + error rate + latency delta). Each row: time, impact icon (color-coded), top symptom tag (timeout | 5xx | model-incoherent), sample token-length, and quick actions (ack, snooze, open).
- Center pane (signal canvas / timeline): multi-track sparkline view over selected time window. Tracks (top-to-bottom): request rate, p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, retry rate, kv-cache-miss-rate, model-variant-switches. Hover shows correlated vertical marker with clickable sample snapshots. Zoom/pan, and ability to pin a vertical marker to freeze sample.
- Right pane (investigation card): tabbed view with 3 tabs — Summary, Samples, and Causal Traces.
  - Summary: auto-generated one-line synopsis (e.g. "Spike in p95 on 2025-02-11; KV cache miss + model-variant flip; 42% of failing requests are long context (>2k tokens)"). Also shows top hypotheses (auto-suggested) and a set of recommended mitigations with risk/latency tradeoff estimates.
  - Samples: rotating set of sanitized request/response pairs. For model errors, show both raw output and a simplified diff from typical output (if we have golden prompt). Provide a replay button that can run a request against a fallback model/variant in a sandbox.
  - Causal Traces: condensed trace list where each trace row highlights the problematic span (e.g. "KV fetch 95ms", "GPU OOM on host-x: container restart"). Allow deep-link to full trace in observability product.

Bottom control bar (actions):
- Quickfix buttons: Retry (with exponential backoff), Route to fallback (choose variant), Reduce max-tokens, Force-cold-start, Toggle caching off/on for this route, Request synthetic replay. Each action shows an estimated change in cost and latency and requires justification for production runs.
- Annotation input: quick tag, short note, assign owner, severity override. Notes get appended to incident metadata and feed downstream RCA.

Interaction flows (common scenarios):
1) Timeout burst during peak traffic:
  - User filters to high severity incidents -> picks top incident -> canvas shows p95 spike aligned with an internal deploy (model-variant switch). Samples show truncated outputs and high token counts.
  - Suggested mitigation: route 30% traffic to previous stable variant + increase request timeout to 15s for canary users.
  - User clicks "Route to fallback" -> chooses variant -> console posts an operation with an audit log entry (action is reversible).

2) 5xx due to infra flakiness:
  - Canvas shows elevated 5xx but no model-variant churn and KV cache healthy. Traces show GPU driver restart events.
  - Suggested mitigation: shift traffic regionally, drain nodes in problematic pool, escalate to infra with trace id.

3) Model output regression (semantic):
  - Samples tab shows higher BLEU/ROUGE deltas vs baseline and a human flag in prior evals. Right pane suggests rolling back to previous model or adjusting prompt.
  - Replay sandbox lets product quickly test prompt tweaks and show delta on a golden suite.

Sample micro-copy and UI copy notes (tone + safety):
- Impact score label: "User impact: medium (12 users/hr)" — avoid alarmist language.
- Replay confirmation: "This sandboxed replay will only hit diagnostic infra and is read-only to customer data."
- Mitigation CTA: show cost delta and who can approve (permission gating).
- Annotation defaults: keep the first line short; treat it as a title in timelines.

Backlog grooming (tickets / prioritized items):
- SCRUB-01: Autogenerated one-line synopsis (NLP model that summarizes correlated signals). Priority: P0 for console-beta. Estimate: 5 pts. Acceptance: 80% of incidents have a synopsis that matches at least one human-written label during trial.
- SCRUB-02: Sandbox replay runner with model/variant toggle (safe env). Priority: P0. Estimate: 8 pts. Acceptance: replay runs deterministically < 30s and has explicit audit log.
- SCRUB-03: KV cache miss rate metric and chart integration. Priority: P1. Estimate: 3 pts. Acceptance: show per-route and global rates; alertable.
- SCRUB-04: One-click route-to-fallback with rollout decay and auto-fallback. Priority: P0. Estimate: 13 pts. Acceptance: role-based control, revert path, audit trail.
- SCRUB-05: Sample diff visualization for model output vs baseline. Priority: P1. Estimate: 5 pts. Acceptance: show token-level diff and quality delta.
- SCRUB-06: Replay permissions + safe-guard modal copy + cost estimate. Priority: P2. Estimate: 2 pts.
- SCRUB-07: Incident impact scoring alpha (volume * error-rate * business-score). Priority: P1. Estimate: 4 pts.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How much of the latency / error provenance do we surface vs link to traces? (clutter vs context) Suggestion: keep 1–2 key spans inline, deep-link to trace viewer.
- Should we auto-run cheap replays (e.g., deterministic prompts) or require explicit user action? Risk: noisy cost and noisy false positives. Preference: manual by default, opt-in for automated watchlists.
- Model outputs may contain PII even after sanitization. Need a policy for what fields are replayable in sandbox. Work with privacy/compliance.
- Impact scoring needs product/business input for weightings (user-facing vs internal-only endpoints).

Accessibility and performance notes:
- Canvas must be performant for 30k events/hour windows; downsample responsibly and show sampling rate.
- Color choices: use combined color + pattern for users with color-vision deficiencies.

Telemetry & analytics we need to capture:
- Which quick fixes are used and their success rate (did errors stop?).
- Time-to-first-action for incidents.
- Frequency of sandbox replays and cost per replay.
- Annotation churn and signal-tag concordance (use to train synopsis model).

Next steps & owners:
- UX: rough mocks in Figma (Maya) — due 2025-01-24.
- Backend: define minimal signal API and a lightweight incident scoring endpoint (Rory) — proto by 2025-01-31.
- Infra/SRE: scope trace deep-linking & RBAC for route changes (Dmitri) — feed into ENG-904.
- Legal/Privacy: draft replay PII policy and sandbox constraints (Kate Williams) — initial review by 2025-02-05.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep initial surface small: start with timeouts + 5xx + model-incoherence, then expand to embeddings / reranking false positives.
- Avoid over-automation in beta — manual steps help collect signal about good heuristics.
- This board should pair with Optimize recommendations in a follow-up (cost/quality tradeoff suggestions).

Mockup checklist (deliverables for next design pass):
- Full-width canvas mock with zoom state and pinned-sample modal.
- Right-pane tab variants (Summary / Samples / Traces) with copy examples.
- Action modal flows for Route-to-fallback (confirm, choose traffic %, schedule rollback).
- Annotation timeline playback where notes are shown inline with canvas markers.

If you want to play with a strawman flow, open the attached Figma link (Maya) and try the "Canary spikes" board — it contains pre-populated sample incidents.

-- end --
